references.text: John's disciples refer to what happened "on the other side of the Jordan" – this points back to [ref:Joh 1:28|John 1:28], where John baptized in Bethany on the other side of the Jordan, the place where Jesus first came to him.

The disciples say "you have testified about him" (σὺ μεμαρτύρηκας). This points back to [ref:Joh 1:7|John 1:7], where it says that John came to testify about the light, so that all might believe through him.

John's testimony about Jesus, which the disciples refer to, is given in detail in [ref:Joh 1:29-34|John 1:29-34], where John points to Jesus as "the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world" and declares that he is the Son of God.

The background for the disciples' concern is described in [ref:Joh 3:22-23|John 3:22-23]: Both Jesus and John were baptizing in the same area – Jesus in Judea and John at Aenon near Salim – which created a competitive situation in the eyes of the disciples.

The situation described here – that Jesus attracted more disciples than John – is explained further in [ref:Joh 4:1-2|John 4:1-2], where it clarifies that the Pharisees heard that Jesus was gaining and baptizing more disciples than John (although Jesus himself did not baptize, but his disciples).
The term "Rabbi" (Ῥαββί) used for John the Baptist shows that his disciples regarded him as their teacher, just as Jesus was addressed as "Rabbi" in [ref:Joh 1:38|John 1:38].
John's answer to this concern comes in [ref:Joh 3:30|John 3:30], where he says "He must increase, but I must decrease" – an expression that it is God's plan for all to come to Jesus.

John's testimony which the disciples refer to includes his declaration in [ref:Joh 1:15|John 1:15], where he cried out: "It was about him I said: He who comes after me has surpassed me, because he was before me."

John answers his disciples in [ref:Joh 3:27-28|John 3:27-28] by reminding them that a person can receive nothing unless it is given to him from heaven, and that he himself said he is not the Messiah, but was sent ahead of him.

Jesus himself later refers to John's testimony in [ref:Joh 5:33-35|John 5:33-35], where he says that John testified to the truth and was a lamp that burned and shone – an affirmation of the testimony the disciples refer to.
